title: Family files federal lawsuit after El Paso man dies in police custody during mental health crisis
text:
Family files federal lawsuit after El Paso man dies in police custody during mental health crisis
The family of Xavier Hernandez, who died in El Paso police custody, filed a federal lawsuit alleging officers used excessive force, including tasing him and holding him prone during a mental health crisis.
According to KVIA, the incident occurred on July 13, 2025, when officers responded to a highway overpass on Interstate 10. Police tased Hernandez and held him prone while applying body weight to his back and neck for nearly 10 minutes. The El Paso County medical examiner ruled the death a homicide caused by oxygen deprivation from chest compression.
Attorneys said Hernandez asked officers for help and showed he was unarmed before being tased, KVIA reported. El Paso Police Department policies required de-escalation techniques and empathy when responding to mental health crises. No criminal charges were filed against the officers and three separate investigations were opened, including one by the Texas Rangers.
A Reuters investigation found more than 1,000 taser-related deaths in the United States since 2000. Amnesty International reported that at least 500 people died after being tased by police between 2001 and 2012 and that 90% of those who died were unarmed at the time.
The El Paso Police Department serves approximately 680,000 residents in the largest city on the Texas-Mexico border, according to the department.
